data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms as a non-inductive, strategic imperative to maximize the rate of error elimination, not as an inference to probable truth.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the goal of science shifts from error elimination to predictive reliability for engineering safety, this strategic defense collapses without an inductive bridge.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'severity' of tests cannot be defined independently of the theory being tested, the metric for 'better-corroborated' becomes circular.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reframing scientific action as a game of 'maximal risk exposure': choosing the theory that has survived the most severe tests is equivalent to choosing the weapon with the highest known durability in battle, not because it is 'magically immune' to future damage (induction), but because it is the only rational bet for surviving the next immediate engagement given the goal of eliminating error. The 'cost' is accepting that this preference offers no guarantee of future success or proximity to truth, only the best available method for exposing falsity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
